Targeted maximum likelihood for a randomised trial

Source: R/rcttml.R
rcttml.Rd

The average treatment effect of a randomised trial with adjustment for baseline covariates by targeted maximum likelihood (Moore and van der Laan 2009): more precise than the difference in means when the covariates predict the outcome, and consistent whatever the outcome model, since the chance of treatment is known by design.

Usage

rcttml(
  data,
  y,
  d,
  x = NULL,
  fam = c("gaussian", "binomial"),
  inter = FALSE,
  g = NULL,
  gx = FALSE,
  gbound = 0.01,
  bounds = NULL,
  qbound = 0.005,
  level = 0.95
)

# S3 method for class 'rcttml'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per participant of the trial.

y

The name of the outcome column (numbers; 0 or 1 for "binomial").

d

The name of the treatment column: 0 or 1 (or FALSE, TRUE), each arm with two participants or more.

x

NULL or the names of the baseline covariate columns (numbers); for print(), an object of class rcttml.

fam

"gaussian" or "binomial".

inter

TRUE to let the effect vary with the covariates in Q.

g

NULL (the share treated) or the known chance of treatment: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

gx

TRUE to fit the chance of treatment on x.

gbound

The bound of g, from 0 to below 0.5.

bounds

NULL (the range of y) or two numbers, below and above every outcome, that put a continuous outcome on [0, 1].

qbound

The bound of the scaled Q, above 0 and below 0.5.

level

The level of the intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

...

Not used by print().

Value

An object of class rcttml, a list: tab, a data frame with rows tmle, gcomp and unadj (method, est, se, lo, hi, p); eps, the fluctuation; g, the smallest and largest chance of treatment used; and fam, bounds, n, level.

Details

The outcome regression Q(d, x) is fitted on an intercept, d and x (and d times each covariate with inter = TRUE): least squares for fam = "gaussian", logistic regression for "binomial" (an outcome of 0 and 1). The chance of treatment g is the trial's share treated (g = NULL), a known value (g), or a logistic regression on x (gx = TRUE), bounded to [gbound, 1 - gbound]. Q is then fluctuated along the clever covariate H = d / g - (1 - d) / (1 - g) by a logistic regression with offset logit(Q); a continuous outcome is first put on [0, 1] by bounds (its range by default) and Q kept in [qbound, 1 - qbound] (Gruber and van der Laan 2010). The effect is the mean of Q*(1, x) - Q*(0, x), its standard error that of the influence curve, sd(IC) / sqrt(n). The table also gives the plug-in of the unfluctuated Q (gcomp, without a standard error) and the difference in means (unadj, with the unpooled standard error); intervals and p-values are normal.

References

Moore, K. L. and van der Laan, M. J. (2009). Covariate adjustment in randomized trials with binary outcomes: targeted maximum likelihood estimation. Statistics in Medicine, 28(1), 39-64. doi:10.1002/sim.3445

Gruber, S. and van der Laan, M. J. (2010). A targeted maximum likelihood estimator of a causal effect on a bounded continuous outcome. The International Journal of Biostatistics, 6(1), 26. doi:10.2202/1557-4679.1260

van der Laan, M. J. and Rubin, D. (2006). Targeted maximum likelihood learning. The International Journal of Biostatistics, 2(1), 11. doi:10.2202/1557-4679.1043

Examples

set.seed(10)
n <- 300
d <- data.frame(prior = rpois(n, 2), age = runif(n, 18, 50),
                t = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5))
d$days <- 30 - 6 * d$t + 3 * d$prior - 0.1 * d$age + rnorm(n, sd = 4)
rcttml(d, "days", "t", c("prior", "age"))
#> rcttml: gaussian outcome, 300 participants; targeted maximum likelihood, g-computation and the difference in means
#>  method    est     se     lo     hi         p
#>    tmle -6.454 0.4857 -7.406 -5.502 2.775e-40
#>   gcomp -6.454     NA     NA     NA        NA
#>   unadj -6.760 0.6640 -8.061 -5.459 2.424e-24
d$rearrest <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-1 - 0.6 * d$t + 0.4 * d$prior))
rcttml(d, "rearrest", "t", "prior", fam = "binomial")$tab
#>   method        est         se         lo          hi           p
#> 1   tmle -0.1443982 0.05330437 -0.2488729 -0.03992356 0.006749907
#> 2  gcomp -0.1443982         NA         NA          NA          NA
#> 3  unadj -0.1570057 0.05574479 -0.2662635 -0.04774791 0.004854871
